llm.summary: The AI trade is splitting cleanly in two and today's tape proves it: Nvidia shipped a product blitz (RTX Spark laptops running 74B Nemotron agents locally, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Adobe/ServiceNow/Honeywell/Navan deployments, a German national AI partnership, and an orbital data-centre tie-up with SpaceX) while CoreWeave sank again pre-market and investors kept dumping data-centre bonds on what the FT calls a 'Darwin moment.' Demand is not the problem; the cost and availability of capital for leveraged compute intermediaries is. Rates are the second axis: September PPI was the hottest in 4.5 years, CPI the hottest since COVID, retail sales beat only because gasoline got expensive, and brokerages still carry a December HIKE — yet Treasuries are heading for their best week since February because the bid is flight-to-safety out of AI equities, not disinflation. Warsh gave no rate signal and praised global tightening, which leaves the hawkish path intact. Gold holds near $4,170 on a softer dollar and easier real yields, while copper logs a third straight daily loss on hike bets — the hard-asset complex is discriminating between monetary hedge and cyclical metal. The power leg keeps hardening into contract: Venture Global targeting 10 GW of gas-fired generation for data centres, Google funding 890 MW of PJM nuclear uprates, Urenco enrichment at 75% — 'bring your own power' is now the default architecture. Both our portfolio growth names gapped up (CRM +4.6%, DXCM +5.1%), and five regional banks report today, which is the cleanest live read on whether the gasoline-squeezed consumer is cracking. Breadth remains the quiet warning: the S&P rally lacks participation, small-cap flows are negative, and Financials/Real Estate/Materials flows are deeply negative into a possible hike.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: this is a credit-led, not rates-led, drawdown with a reflexive bounce on top. Yields falling into a 6%+ PPI print is collateral rotation; if the 2-year reverses once the equity panic fades, today's duration relief in DXCM, BAX and the long-duration software complex evaporates. I want to be long the AI income statement (chips, on-device inference, agentic software with banked cash flow) and short the AI balance sheet (neoclouds, tier-2 compute, contractors whose backlog depends on a leveraged customer rolling paper). Energy sector rotation at +71 and Technology at +44 against Financials -64 and Real Estate -75 tells you the market is already paying for electrons and compute while refusing to pay for anything rate-sensitive or credit-levered. Bank earnings today (TFC, CFG, RF, MTB, TRV) and the next leg in data-centre spreads are the two swing variables.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: stagflation-lite and reflation are now tied at 27.5 each while Goldilocks collapses -8.1, which is the market's way of saying the distribution has fattened at both tails of the inflation path and thinned in the middle. Pipeline cost at 4.5-year highs either compresses corporate margins or gets pushed to a household already paying for gasoline before goods — that is the trade-down engine for value retail and the squeeze on discretionary. Mortgage rates at a near-three-year high freeze the housing transaction economy into 2027, and public search attention on 'housing market crash' is rising while the theme is flagged not-priced, which is a setup for a sentiment shock before a fundamental one. The AI capex cycle continues but the financing mix migrates from high-yield neocloud debt toward hyperscaler cash flow, utility ratebase and sovereign partnerships (Germany-Nvidia, Taiwan's $4bn Texas hub) — multiple-compressive for AI-adjacent equities, cash-flow-accretive for regulated power, gas and nuclear, which get paid regardless of which model wins.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: the binding constraint on intelligence has moved from chips to capital and electrons, and the toll-takers are the ones who own interconnect, ratebase, enrichment and gas turbines. Second, inference is decentralising — a 74B model running locally on a $2,599 laptop is the start of an on-device compute cycle that re-rates the PC and edge-device supply chain and partially decouples AI adoption from hyperscaler capex, which is a structural hedge against exactly the financing stress now visible in the bond market. Third, this is the first genuine credit cycle of the AI era; as in telecom after 2001 the infrastructure will get used but the owners will change, concentrating the industry into five or six balance sheets. Underneath all of it the household is being repriced from an asset-price economy to an income economy — electricity bill assistance queries, housing-crash searches, gasoline-driven nominal retail sales — permanently favouring affordability, essential health, regulated power, and firms that sell cost removal to businesses rather than aspiration to consumers.

short_term: Consumers are spending more dollars for less stuff: September retail sales beat but the increment went to gasoline, meaning nominal strength masking real-volume weakness — the trade-down to value retail accelerates from here.

Households are treating electricity as a budget line, not a background utility: rising searches for bill assistance, bill calculators and average bills alongside 'power grid emergency' queries across 13 states.

Homebuyers have stepped out of the transaction market at near-three-year-high mortgage rates and are redirecting into maintenance and smaller-ticket DIY — Home Depot's rising average ticket with softer traffic is the signature of fewer, more necessary projects.

Investors are discriminating within the AI trade for the first time: buying Nvidia's pullback as a toll-road while dumping neocloud equity and data-centre bonds, i.e. separating rent collectors from leveraged borrowers.
Capital is choosing gold over crypto as the debasement hedge — gold holds $4,170 on softer dollar and yields while bitcoin only 'enters early recovery' with no independent bid.
Private equity, locked out of IPO exits, is tapping the debt market to pay distributions to LPs — a liquidity workaround that raises system leverage precisely as credit spreads widen.

Enterprises are buying agents rather than seats: Navan, Honeywell, ServiceNow, Adobe all announcing agentic deployments in a single morning means the procurement unit is shifting from software licences to labour substitution.
long_term: Privacy, latency and cost are pushing inference onto the device — local 74B-class agents on consumer laptops change what people expect to own versus rent, and restore a replacement cycle to hardware.

Energy security becomes a corporate function rather than a utility purchase: Venture Global selling 10 GW directly to data centres, Google funding nuclear uprates, Venezuela asking oil firms to bring their own power — 'bring your own electrons' spreads from AI to all heavy industry.
Status and aspiration spending continues to lose share to security and affordability spending; Nike's weak guidance versus value-retail resilience is the same consumer making the same choice.

Strategic stockpiling becomes normal state behaviour — Mercuria's first copper into the US Project Vault, rare-earth magnet capacity answering an Army call, Urenco enrichment expansion — resource access is being treated as a national-security good, not a commodity market.

Work is being reorganised around agents with human oversight rather than human workflows with software assistance; ServiceNow employees building agents under Nvidia oversight is the template for the next decade of white-collar productivity.

Healthcare moves toward continuous monitoring and device-mediated self-management as a hedge against both cost inflation and scarce clinician time — the structural demand under DXCM and the medical-device complex.

Space transitions from launch services to infrastructure: orbital data centres, sovereign alternatives to Starlink after the Ukraine curbs, and defence constellations make orbit a contested utility layer.

portfolio_implications.why: Two fresh, independent tailwinds landed today. First, Nvidia shipping RTX Spark laptops with local 74B agent inference establishes an on-device AI spec that enterprise refresh cycles must chase, and HPQ sells into exactly that fleet. Second, the memory narrative has flipped from scarcity panic to 2029 oversupply, which lowers BOM cost into 2027 gross margin. HPQ also has none of the leveraged-customer credit exposure that is currently repricing the AI complex — it sells to IT budgets, not to neoclouds rolling high-yield paper.

Gapped +4.6% pre-market into a morning that validated the agentic enterprise thesis across Adobe, ServiceNow, Navan and Honeywell. Thesis intact — FCF improving, theme exposure strengthening, valuation below own history — but do not chase a gap in a tape where the S&P rally lacks breadth and Growth is leading Value by 46 points. Let it consolidate; add on a pullback that holds the gap.

Gapped +5.1% on easing yields with Health Care rotation at +34 and improving ROIC, margins and FCF. The caution is that the duration relief driving the gap is a flight-to-safety out of AI equities, not disinflation — PPI was the hottest in 4.5 years and December hike risk is live. The fundamental case (continuous monitoring is payer-funded and recession-resistant) stands on its own; the rate tailwind should not be underwritten.

Defensive medtech with accelerating revenue, improving FCF and a double valuation discount is the right ballast when regime probabilities are a four-way coin flip with Goldilocks collapsing. J&J raising 2026 guidance supports the sector read. Hold, do not size up — the position earns its keep through the stagflation path, not the reflation one.

The weakest link in the book right now. Industrials flows at -50, US-Mexico tariff talks on metals and autos stalling, and the data-centre build-chain markdown all pressure the industrial capex customer base. The offsetting case is edge AI on ruggedised devices, which is real but slower than the thesis assumes. Review sizing against the HPQ edge-AI exposure, which captures the same structural idea with better valuation support and less cyclical capex beta.
